note: Treats poisoning, drift and integrity as one governance problem, which matches how these failures actually present in production.
title: AI governance under threat managing data poisoning, drift, and integrity challenges
explain_beginner: This paper looks at three problems that can hurt AI systems used in business operations. Data poisoning is when bad information gets fed into the system on purpose. Data drift is when the real world changes and the data no longer matches. Data integrity means the data is trustworthy and complete. The authors say these problems are usually studied separately, but in real life they happen together and feed into each other. The paper reviews existing research and builds a framework that combines technical checks, clear accountability inside organisations, and outside oversight, so AI stays reliable over time.
explain_business: For executives, the message is that AI failures in operations rarely come from one isolated technical fault. Poisoned inputs, shifting data patterns and integrity gaps reinforce each other, so treating them as separate IT issues leaves the organisation exposed. The paper offers a governance framework combining technical checks, clear internal accountability and recognised oversight principles across the whole AI lifecycle. The practical decision this informs is how to structure AI oversight, specifically whether to fund continuous data and model assurance and assign ownership, rather than relying only on security tooling. It is most relevant for firms deploying AI in complex, data-heavy supply chain environments.
explain_practitioner: This is a structured narrative review, not an experimental study. The authors synthesise existing literature on data poisoning, data drift and data integrity, which prior work treated separately, and argue they should be governed as one interconnected risk across the AI lifecycle. An illustrative supply chain case scenario shows how these failures interact in operational settings. The main output is an Integrated AI Governance Framework that unifies technical assurance, organisational governance and internationally recognised governance principles within a single lifecycle model. The key claim is that technical safeguards alone are insufficient, continuous lifecycle assurance, data governance, accountability and regulatory oversight are all required.
